mainEntity.name: Are angled dental implants a permanent solution?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dental implants — whether straight or angled — are designed as a long-term tooth replacement solution. With appropriate surgical placement, a well-designed prosthetic restoration, and consistent oral hygiene and professional maintenance, implants can function effectively for many years. That said, no dental treatment comes with a guaranteed permanent outcome, as individual factors including bone health, oral hygiene, and lifestyle habits all play a role in long-term success. A clinical assessment will help establish realistic expectations for your individual circumstances.

The All-on-4 concept, which uses two straight and two angled implants to support a full-arch restoration, has been studied in numerous clinical trials and long-term case series. The available evidence suggests it is a clinically recognised approach for suitable patients. As with any surgical procedure, risks exist, and a thorough pre-treatment assessment is essential to determine suitability. Your implant dentist will discuss potential risks and benefits with you before any treatment proceeds.

mainEntity.name: Will I need a bone graft if I choose angled implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: One of the reasons angled implants are used is to reduce or eliminate the need for bone grafting by accessing areas of the jaw with better bone volume. However, this is not always the case for every patient. Some individuals may still require bone augmentation depending on the extent of bone loss and the specific treatment plan proposed. This determination can only be made following a detailed clinical and radiographic examination, including 3D imaging.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take for angled implants to integrate with the bone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Osseointegration typically takes between eight and twelve weeks, though this can vary depending on factors such as bone density, patient age, and general health. In some full-arch restoration protocols, a provisional restoration is fitted shortly after surgery to restore function during the healing period. The final restoration is usually fitted once osseointegration has been confirmed. Your dental team will provide a timeline tailored to your treatment plan.

mainEntity.name: Can I eat normally with angled dental implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: Once osseointegration is complete and the final restoration is securely fitted, most patients are able to eat a broad range of foods comfortably. During the healing phase, dietary modifications — such as avoiding very hard or chewy foods — are typically advised to protect the implants whilst integration occurs. Your dental team will provide specific guidance appropriate to your treatment.

mainEntity.name: What is peri-implantitis and how can it be prevented?

acceptedAnswer.text: Peri-implantitis is an inflammatory condition affecting the gum tissue and bone surrounding a dental implant, similar in some respects to periodontitis around natural teeth. It is typically caused by the accumulation of bacterial plaque around the implant, often as a result of inadequate oral hygiene. If left untreated, it can lead to bone loss around the implant. Prevention involves diligent daily cleaning around the implant, regular professional hygiene appointments, and avoiding smoking. Early detection during routine monitoring appointments is important for effective management.
